title: Hard-rule fixture register
description: The checked-in register of hard `mode: enforce` critics that have no `active` mutation fixture, and of the ones that have gained one. Constitution Article IV says every hard rule in the registry must ship with a killing fixture; governance section 3 stage 4 says CI must check it. Today that property is false for most of the loaded registry, and the honest way to hold a false property is to count it rather than to name a green check after it. Every hard enforcing critic in every registry the build loads appears exactly once, in `gaps` or in `covered`. A critic in neither fails the check, which is what makes a newly added hard rule loud. A critic in `gaps` whose candidate fixture has become `active` also fails, which is what makes the register shrink-only.

note.description: Why this file exists, for a reader who arrives at it from a red check.

exemption.description: Stage 4 is the one CI stage whose specification says no manual override exists, so the register itself is an exemption and needs an ADR the way a retired fixture does (increment-2 plan section 5.5, decision D-8). Absent until that ADR is written; the checker reports its absence rather than failing, because failing would delete the count.

gap_count.description: The number of entries in `gaps`, restated so the count is data the CI job can print. A green `hard-rules-have-fixtures` check with a non-zero count here means the register is consistent, not that Article IV is satisfied.

gaps.description: Hard enforcing critics with no `active` fixture. May only shrink.

covered.description: Hard enforcing critics that have gained an `active` fixture. An entry moves here from `gaps`, and only with a fixture a reviewer has confirmed exercises this critic's class.

task_id.description: A work-breakdown task identifier from docs/sdd/03-work-breakdown.md.

registry.description: Repository-relative path of the registry document the critic was read from. Named per entry because the check is keyed on every registry the build loads, not on one fixture file: a hard critic added to a second registry must be as visible as one added to the first.

action_class.description: The `tool/intent` pair that declares the critic. One rule identifier can appear in several classes, and a fixture that kills it in one class has not been shown to kill it in another.

source_requirement.description: The critic's declared `source_requirement`, copied from the registry. Checked against the loaded registry, so a renamed requirement shows up here rather than silently detaching the rule from the rule it encodes.

location.description: The fields both lists share: which critic, in which registry document, in which action class, encoding which requirement. `unevaluatedProperties: false` is applied by the two composed definitions rather than here, because `additionalProperties` at this level cannot see the fields the composing schema adds and would reject every entry.

candidate_fixtures.description: The catalogued fixtures that would prove this critic blocks - fixtures whose `expected` names this rule, not every fixture that touches the same requirement. Empty means the catalogue has no fixture for this rule at all, which is the deeper gap: an absence with no identifier cannot be counted. `note` is then required to say so.

proving_fixtures.description: The fixtures that prove this critic blocks. At least one must be declared `active`, or the entry is a claim with nothing behind it.
